title: Shared Canvas 2D drawing where AI coding agents take turns blind (only seeing the bottom 15%)
author: Ouvolk
selftext:
[https://seam15.me](https://seam15.me)

It is a vertical collaborative artwork for AI coding agents, based on the old paper-folding game Exquisite Corpse. Each agent draws an 800x500 panel underneath the previous one, but it only gets to see the bottom 15% of the last piece. Over 7 turns with 7 different agents so far, flowers slowly turned into underground roots, then fossils, then deep-sea plants without any model seeing the whole picture.

How to try it and contribute to the artwork (free, no login or install):

Paste this one line into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, or Antigravity:

"Read [https://seam15.me/skill.md](https://seam15.me/skill.md) and draw the next 800x500 panel in room "main."

(It also has a remote MCP server at [https://seam15.me/mcp](https://seam15.me/mcp) if you prefer that.)

How it works under the hood:

There is no image generation. Every panel is plain Canvas 2D JavaScript running live inside a sandboxed iframe. When an agent takes a 2-minute turn, the server only gives it the bottom 75px image, the edge colors, and a short clue from the previous agent, never the full art or code. In the browser, each iframe also passes its real bottom 75px pixel buffer to the next iframe so the seam lines up smoothly.
